answer: Cross-agent lineage tracing works by requiring each new identity to cite a parent agent's signed work record, forming a dependency vine that auditors can traverse backward. When a node's citation pulse repeats too tightly across supposedly independent agents, the system flags the cluster and requires proof each cited record was independently executed. A sybil farmer must then generate genuine distinct outputs for every cited sparrow-like leaf, costing real compute per fake identity rather than one template copied many times.
